messages:
Maya: Heads up — seeing degraded NCCL throughput and occasional hangs on multi-GPU jobs in g5-dedicated us-west-2. Tail latency for allreduce spikes to seconds. :grimacing:
Owen: Which cluster and which pods? recent deploy?
Maya: g5-pool-prod-02, mostly 8xA100-style jobs (nccl allreduce rings). No deploys at the same time. Started ~2h ago after autoscale bump.
Maya: I grabbed dmesg and the mlx counters — see snippets below:
Maya: ```
mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: pfc_pause: class0_flaps=12 class1_flaps=0 class2_flaps=3
ib_core: qp 0x1b state=ERR last_wqe=42
kernel: xdp: dropped pkts due to MTU fragment=1248
```
Anika: pfc flaps + qp ERR is a red flag for PFC storm/backpressure chain deadlock. Are we seeing pause frames on the leaf?
Maya: Yes, leaf1 shows class0 pause bursts, matched timestamps with job slowdowns.
Owen: Can you run `ibv_devinfo -v` and `ethtool -S <iface>` on one affected host? Also a short tcpdump on UDP port 4791 (RoCEv2) would help.
Maya: Ran quick checks, pasted outputs:
Maya: ```
# ibv_devinfo -v
device: mlx5_0
port: 1
state: PORT_ACTIVE
max_qp: 32768
sm_lid: 0
# ethtool -S ens5 | grep pfc
mlx5_fc_pfc_event_class0: 14
mlx5_fc_pfc_event_class2: 4
# tcpdump -n -c 50 -w - udp port 4791 | tcpdump -r -
  IP 10.0.1.5.4791 > 10.0.1.6.4791: UDP, length 1280
  IP 10.0.1.5.4791 > 10.0.1.6.4791: UDP, length 1400  <-- larger than MTU
```
Liam: Looks like UDP fragmentation — some packets > MTU causing drops. RoCEv2 uses UDP so fragmented packets can be lost if switches don't reassemble. Could be MTU mismatch or offload mismatch on the host side.
Anika: Also seeing QP state transitions to ERR which matches packet loss. When RoCE packets are dropped mid-stream, NIC/driver can surface qp errors.
Owen: Try: 1) check switch MTU on path, 2) check if GRO/TSO offloads are fragmenting the RoCE UDP frames, 3) temporarily reduce NCCL MTU/ring size to avoid >1500 UDP datagrams.
Maya: I disabled TSO/GSO on the host iface and re-ran a small allreduce test — throughput recovered for ~10m then flapped again when another queued job started.
Maya: Commands I used:
Maya: ```
ip link set dev ens5 tso off gso off gro off
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; run_small_allreduce.sh
```
sre-bot: Incident INC-1234 opened: nccl-throughput-usw2, assigned: Owen + Anika. Pager duty: infra oncall.
Owen: Can infra check if any ECN/PFC policy changes rolled out to leaf1/leaf2 in the last 24h? Also dump QoS and mirror counters for the fabric.
infra-ops-bot: Config change log: no ACLs or QoS changes in last 24h. However, firmware push to leaf1 was applied 3h ago (fw v7.3.2 -> v7.4.0).
Anika: Firmware could change PFC handling defaults. If PFC is flapping we get backpressure cascades. Suggest enabling lossless isolation class for NCCL traffic (class 3) and rate-limit other classes.
Liam: Short-term mitigation: move affected jobs to g5-pool-standby in a different AZ (us-west-2b). Longer-term: pin NIC firmware or roll forward fixes and validate MTU consistent across fabric.
Maya: Moved a batch of jobs to standby — success for those jobs. Still seeing intermittent hangs for jobs that stayed on original nodes.
Owen: Let's also try NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to bind to specific interface and set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=0/1 tests to understand whether GPUDirect is making it worse.
Maya: Ran nccl tests with NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 (fallback tcp): no hangs, lower peak perf but stable. With IB enabled, higher perf but intermittent hangs.
Anika: That confirms a RoCE/ibverbs stack issue. Next steps: 1) repro with packet capture through leaf switch, 2) open vendor ticket (Mellanox) with firmware diff, 3) schedule a firmware rollback window if vendor confirms regression.
Owen: Also we should consider enabling UDP segmentation offload patch that avoids >MTU RoCE datagrams (we saw one 1400 sample) — or set NIC to not coalesce NCCL flows.
Maya: I'll collect full pkt captures and the mlx logs and attach to INC-1234. Estimated impact: ~4-8 concurrent jobs affected, tail latency increase causing several customer slowdowns.
infra-ops-bot: Capacity note: g5-pool-standby has ~12% spare capacity; provisioning request queued if we need more.
Liam: Cost tradeoff: scaling up reserved pool would mitigate blast radius but increases monthly committed spend. Ops, is there a quick mitigation we can roll globally?
Anika: Global mitigation: enforce MTU=9000 across fabric + consistent offload settings via bootstrap config, and set NCCL env defaults to prefer smaller UDP frames for cross-host allreduce. That requires coordination but reduces frag rate.
Maya: For now, I'll cordon the most affected hosts and route new jobs to standby. Collecting artifacts now, will update INC-1234 with pcaps and ibv logs. :thumbsup:
Owen: Thanks — once we have vendor feedback we can decide firmware rollback vs config mitigation.
Maya: Closing loop: posted logs & pcaps to the ticket. Will follow up in the incident thread with vendor ticket ID.
